tasks.short: Question patrons about the services they want and the haircut style.

steps.what: Question patrons regarding the desired services and the haircut styles.
Write the requested services and the haircut style as her own note.

tasks.design: She questions each patron about the services they want and the haircut style, then writes that request as her own note. The words are spoken at the chair. Nothing is drafted for her and nothing is filed for her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The request is spoken at the chair and changes with the hair she can see.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing in the till or the books hears that conversation, so it stays with her.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the style the patron actually wants.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the style and can see whether it suits the hair in front of her.
tasks.altitude: Her week on this task does not change. She still questions patrons and writes the requested services herself. Nothing is drafted.

There is no structured-input contract. The patron speaks the request. She writes the note herself, as she does today.
Nothing is drafted, so there is no gate and no release. Incremental upkeep is zero because she keeps no new record.

tasks.short: Record the services on the cashier ticket and take the customer's payment.

steps.what: Record the services provided on the cashiers' tickets.
Receive payment from the customers for that ticket.

tasks.design: She records the services provided on the cashier ticket, then takes the payment from the customer in person. The ticket is not written by a machine. The customer hands her the money at the chair.
tasks.previous_blocker: The customer is at the chair and pays for the services she just did.
tasks.enabler_now: A till can hold a total, but it does not take the money out of the customer's hand.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing that the payment matches the ticket she is holding.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person the customer pays, and she can see the ticket and the money together.
tasks.altitude: Her week on this task does not change. She still writes the cashier ticket and takes the payment in person.

tasks.short: Hire and supervise staff, keep the other records, and pay the shop's bills.

steps.what: Do the hiring and supervising of personnel in the shop.
Perform the clerical and administrative duties of keeping records other than the bills.
Prepare bill amounts v1 from the bank feed and the till export.
Check bill amounts v1 and reject an amount that is not a bill she is paying.
Enter the checked bill amounts v1 in the books.
Continue paying the bills herself once the books hold the checked amounts.

tasks.design: She hires and supervises the shop and keeps the other records herself. A draft step prepares bill amounts v1 from the bank feed on the {BANK} and the till export on the {OTHER}; she checks that each amount is a bill she is paying; a separate release enters that checked version in the {ERP}. She still pays the supplier herself. The draft is not gated and does not pay anyone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier amounts sat in the bank feed and she retyped them into the books, while hiring stayed a conversation in the shop.
tasks.enabler_now: The bank feed already holds the amount and the bill date, so the books can be configured to take bill amounts v1 after she checks them.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a supplier bill from takings, and hiring the people she will supervise.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which bills she is paying and who should work in the shop.
tasks.altitude: She still hires and supervises, still keeps the other records, and still pays suppliers. She checks bill amounts before they are filed, and she no longer types an amount the bank feed already holds.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of personal service workers
reach.task: Stay on the floor while staff are hired and supervised.
reach.learn: Who is already on the floor in the week she is hiring.

evidence.claim: A bank feed and a till export can copy amounts into the books without a model.
The business keeps its administration, bills and receipts for seven years.
A works council is required from 50 staff.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is hiring, supervising, the other records, bill amounts v1, the check, the books filing, and her own payment. It does not cover the visit note or the haircut.

Named fields are supplier, amount, and bill date. The bank feed on the {BANK} produces the amount and the date. The till export on the {OTHER} produces the takings amount, which is not a supplier bill. If an amount is empty the draft does not run and she writes that field inside the check.

The draft is not gated and adds no new bill. The check reads bill amounts v1 after it exists and rejects an amount that is not a bill she is paying, including takings. If she rejects, the release does not file that version.

The release enters that same version and does not write a new one and does not pay a supplier. The payment reuses the check. It is a send of money outside the organisation. It does not wait for a later check of the payment itself. A later edit voids the check.
Test the native books on the {ERP} before custom code. Existing bank-feed and till runtime is not her effort. A missing amount is corrected inside the check, so incremental upkeep is zero.

The in-person step is 59 because the in-person means share is 58.1. The records step is 14 because the document means share is 13.5. The four screen steps are 8, 8, 4 and 7 because screens, mail and the workbook share add to 28.4.
This employer has 200 to 2,000 staff, so a works council exists. Access still needs that consultation. Bills and receipts stay for seven years. The design does not delete them.
unknowns: Whether the bank feed already separates supplier bills from takings.
research_questions: Which amounts on the bank feed are supplier bills this shop pays?

already_counted.description: She checks bill amounts v1 and rejects an amount that is not a bill she is paying.

incremental.description: A missing amount is written inside the check, so there is no extra upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a week where the feed has no supplier amount, so the copy does not run. High is a week where the feed holds the amounts and she still types a few by hand.

tasks.short: Keep the client card after each visit, with the note, the products and the fee.

steps.what: Stay with the clientele after each visit while the card files are kept.
Type her recording of the notes of work done on the card files.
Assemble visit charge v1 from the till checkout as the products used and the fees charged.
Check visit charge v1 so the products and the fees charged match this visit.
File the checked visit charge v1 on the client card files.

tasks.design: She stays with the clientele and types the note of work done herself. Checkout on the {OTHER} writes the products and the fee into visit charge v1; she checks that they match this visit; a separate release files that checked version on the client card in the {CRM}. The draft does not type the note and does not add health data.
tasks.previous_blocker: She retyped the products and the fee onto the card after checkout, and the note of work done was still her own words.
tasks.enabler_now: The till checkout already holds the products and the fee, so the client record can be configured to take visit charge v1 after she checks them.
tasks.still_hard: The note of work done is her own words, and a product the till did not store still needs her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows whether the products and the fee belong to this visit, and what the work was.
tasks.altitude: She still stays with the clientele and still types the note of work done. She checks products and the fee before they are filed on the client card, and she no longer types a product the till already holds.

reach.task: Record the colour formula and the product used after a colour service.
reach.learn: Which product name the colour formula uses, so her note of work done stays hers.

evidence.claim: A salon client record holds treatment notes and purchase history.
Checkout can copy the products and the fee onto that record without a model. She still types the note.
Notes on skin conditions, allergies or reactions to dye are health data.
The business keeps its administration, bills and receipts for seven years.
A works council is required from 50 staff.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is the time with the clientele after the visit, her note of work done, visit charge v1, the check, and the filing on the client card. It does not cover the haircut, the cashier ticket, or paying a supplier.
Named fields are the products and the fee. The till checkout on the {OTHER} produces both. If either field is empty the draft does not run and she writes that field inside the check.

The draft is not gated. It adds no note and no health data. Skin conditions, allergies and dye reactions stay off this note unless consent already exists. The check reads visit charge v1 after it exists and rejects a product or a fee that is not this visit. The release files that same version and does not write a new one. A later edit voids the check.
The release is a write inside the organisation. It does not send a receipt outside. It does not type the note.

Test the native client record on the {CRM} before custom code. Existing till and client-record runtime is not her effort. A product or fee the checkout did not hold is written inside the check, so incremental upkeep is zero.

The in-person step is 45 because the in-person means share is 45.0. The note is 48 because the document means share is 47.7. The checkout copy, the check and the filing are 3, 2 and 2 because screens, mail and the workbook share add to 7.2.

This employer has 200 to 2,000 staff, so a works council exists. Access still needs that consultation. Fees that are kept are administration and stay for seven years. The design does not delete them. There is no time clock and no booking chatbot.
